resources.string: Encrypt files that only this vault can open

Encrypted files stay wherever you save them: on this phone, a USB drive or cloud storage. Only the key is kept in the vault, so it moves with your encrypted backups and phone transfers. Files use the open age format, so the age tool on a computer can open them too.
PassVault makes a post-quantum key and saves it in your vault. Nobody can open the files without it: not by guessing, and not with a future quantum computer.
The encrypted file keeps its name, which anyone can see. Rename it when you save if the name says too much.
Share this to encrypt files for this vault on a computer (age 1.3 or later: age -r KEY). It can only encrypt, not decrypt, so it is safe to share.
Every key here can decrypt files. New files use the newest key. Keep older keys, or the files encrypted with them can no longer be opened.
Your file key is only on this phone. Back up the vault so you can still open your files if you lose it.

PassVault adds a \"File encryption key\" entry to your vault. Files you encrypt can only be opened with it. If you lose this phone and have no encrypted backup or transferred copy of the vault, those files can never be opened by anyone, including you.

New files will be encrypted with the new key. Your current key stays in the vault so older files still open. Only one key is needed; make another one only if you want to stop using the current one, for example after sharing its secret key.
I understand and will back up my vault
PassVault uses this key to decrypt files you encrypted. If you delete it, those files can no longer be opened.
File encryption key created. Back up your vault now.
That key is already in your vault.
Paste an age secret key (AGE-SECRET-KEY-1… or AGE-SECRET-KEY-PQ-1…), for example one made with age-keygen. Files encrypted to it can then be opened here.
This is not an age secret key.
\"%1$s\" was saved encrypted. The original file is still there and is not encrypted. Delete it?
The app holding the original does not allow deleting it from here. Delete it there.
Decrypted copy saved. It is not protected: delete it when you are done.
The file could not be processed. Nothing was saved.
This is not an encrypted file PassVault or age can open.
This file was not encrypted with any key in this vault.
The file is damaged or was changed after it was encrypted. Nothing was saved.
This entry is your file encryption key. Encrypted files open only while it is in the vault. It cannot be edited.
\"%1$s\" is a file encryption key. Files encrypted with it can never be opened again, unless you still have a backup that contains it.
This includes a file encryption key. Files encrypted with it can never be opened again, unless you still have a backup that contains it.
